title: The Influence of Ceiling Height: The Effect of Priming on the Type of Processing That People Use

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.mechanism: high ceiling primes freedom-related concepts
findings.quote: individuals in a high versus low ceiling room reported being in a higher freedom body state (Mhigh = 5.11, Mlow = 4.29; F(1, 28) = 4.48, p < .05)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.mechanism: low ceiling primes confinement-related concepts
findings.quote: but a lower confinement-related body state (Mhigh = 1.89, Mlow = 3.00; F(1,28) = 7.69, p < .01)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.mechanism: high ceiling primes freedom-related concepts, facilitating processing of related words
findings.quote: Participants in the high versus low ceiling room exhibited faster RT to freedom-related anagrams (Mhigh = 8,038.69, Mlow = 14,187.02; F(1, 28) = 4.50, p < .05)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.mechanism: low ceiling primes confinement-related concepts, facilitating processing of related words
findings.quote: yet slower RT to confinement-related anagrams (Mhigh = 14,988.18, Mlow = 10,168.69; F(1, 28) = 5.56, p < .03)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.mechanism: priming effects are specific to related concepts
findings.quote: and comparable RT to unrelated anagrams (Mhigh = 10,449.08, Mlow = 9,408.08; F < 1)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* high ceiling-height salience (lanterns hung from ceiling)
findings.consequent: total number of dimensions generated (categorization task)
findings.mechanism: high ceiling primes freedom, leading to relational processing and more shared dimensions
findings.quote: when the salience of the ceiling height was relatively high... participants in the high versus low ceiling condition produced a larger number of dimensions (F(1, 95) = 11.93, p < .001)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* low ceiling-height salience (lanterns at eye level)
findings.consequent: total number of dimensions generated (categorization task)
findings.mechanism: low salience prevents priming effect
findings.quote: These differences were absent, however, when the salience of the ceiling height was low (p's >.21)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* high ceiling-height salience (lanterns hung from ceiling)
findings.consequent: degree of abstraction of dimensions (categorization task)
findings.mechanism: high ceiling primes freedom, leading to relational processing and more abstract ideation
findings.quote: greater abstraction in the sports dimensions that they identified (F(1,95) = 6.00, p < .05)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* low ceiling-height salience (lanterns at eye level)
findings.consequent: degree of abstraction of dimensions (categorization task)
findings.mechanism: low salience prevents priming effect
findings.quote: These differences were absent, however, when the salience of the ceiling height was low (p's >.21)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* high ceiling-height salience (lanterns hung from ceiling)
findings.consequent: average number of subgroups per dimension (categorization task)
findings.mechanism: high ceiling primes freedom, leading to relational processing and more inclusive categories (fewer subgroups)
findings.quote: and a smaller average number of subgroups per dimension (F(1,95) = 4.73, p < .05)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* low ceiling-height salience (lanterns at eye level)
findings.consequent: average number of subgroups per dimension (categorization task)
findings.mechanism: low salience prevents priming effect
findings.quote: These differences were absent, however, when the salience of the ceiling height was low (p's >.21)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* high ceiling-height salience (lanterns hung from ceiling)
findings.mechanism: high ceiling primes freedom, leading to relational processing, emphasizing commonalities (sleekness) over crude features
findings.quote: when the salience of the ceiling height was high, participants in high versus low ceiling rooms evaluated both the coffee-table (F(1,95) = 4.55, p < .05)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* low ceiling-height salience (lanterns at eye level)
findings.mechanism: low salience prevents priming effect
findings.quote: However, when ceiling-height salience was low, such differences in product evaluation were absent (p's > .22).

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* high ceiling-height salience (lanterns hung from ceiling)
findings.mechanism: high ceiling primes freedom, leading to relational processing, emphasizing commonalities (sleekness) over crude features
findings.quote: and the wine rack (F(1,95) = 8.11, p < .01) as more sleek.

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet) *moderated by* low ceiling-height salience (lanterns at eye level)
findings.mechanism: low salience prevents priming effect
findings.quote: However, when ceiling-height salience was low, such differences in product evaluation were absent (p's > .22).

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.mechanism: high ceiling primes freedom, leading to relational processing
findings.quote: those in a high versus low ceiling room exhibited more recall clustering (i.e., higher ARC scores), indicating the use of greater relational processing (Mhigh = .74, Mlow = .49; F(1,31) = 4.96, p < .05)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.consequent: items recalled per category during cued recall
findings.mechanism: low ceiling primes confinement, leading to item-specific processing
findings.quote: participants in a low versus high ceiling room identified more items during cued recall, indicating greater reliance on item-specific elaboration (Mhigh = 2.80, Mlow = 3.33; F(1, 31) = 4.13, p < .05)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.mechanism: high ceiling primes freedom-related concepts
findings.quote: participants in a high versus low ceiling room reported that they felt a greater freedom-related state (Mhigh = 5.08, Mlow = 4.14; F(1, 31) = 7.92, p < .01)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.mechanism: low ceiling primes confinement-related concepts
findings.quote: but a lower confinement-related state (Mhigh = 2.18, Mlow = 3.22; F(1, 31) = 5.42, p < .05)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.mechanism: ceiling height affects freedom-related body state, which in turn affects ARC scores
findings.quote: the effect of ceiling height on ARC scores was mediated by participants' freedom-related state (bch = .05 [ch = ceiling height], p = .69; b free = .15 [free = freedom], p < .05; Sobel: Z = 2.00, p < .05)

findings.antecedent: ceiling height (high: 10 feet vs. low: 8 feet)
findings.consequent: items recalled per category during cued recall
findings.mechanism: ceiling height affects confinement-related body state, which in turn affects cued recall
findings.quote: the effect of ceiling height on the cued recall measure was mediated by participants' confinement-related state (bch = -.22, p = .41; bcon = .25 [con = confinement], p < .01; Sobel Z = -1.86, p < .06)

findings.antecedent: confinement-related body state
findings.mechanism: confinement-related body state did not mediate ARC scores
findings.quote: Note that participants' confinement-related body state did not mediate ARC scores (bch = .28, p < .05; bcon = .06, p > .18)

findings.antecedent: freedom-related body state
findings.consequent: items recalled per category during cued recall
findings.mechanism: freedom-related body state did not mediate cued recall
findings.quote: and their freedom-related state did not mediate cued recall (bch = -.77, p < .05, bfree = .24, p > .11).

stimuli.description: four identical rooms, two with 10-foot ceilings (high), two with 8-foot false ceilings (low). Colorful Chinese lanterns hung from the ceiling to enhance salience.
stimuli.source: Method section, Appendix A (Fig A1), Appendix B (Fig B1)

stimuli.description: photos of a coffee-table and a wine rack, chosen for sleek appearance with some crude features

tables.description: Treatment means and standard deviations for Experiment 2 measures (categorization task, product evaluation)

limitations: Uncertainty if findings generalize to extreme spatial volume contexts (extremely low or high ceilings).
Uncertainty if typical stores without explicit salience cues (like lanterns) would elicit similar effects.
Possibility that high/low ceilings could prime opposite concepts (confinement vs. freedom) under certain circumstances.
